item.title: BB warns against 22 unauthorized online payment platforms
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank on Sunday issued a public warning notice identifying 22 unlicensed online payment platforms operating in the country and urging the public to refrain from using or participating in their activities.
According to the central bank's Payment Systems Supervision Department, providing payment services or operating a payment system without a valid license from Bangladesh Bank violates Section 4(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, and is punishable under Section 37(1) of the same act.
The department identified the following 22 platforms providing payment aggregator services without statutory approval: BohudurPay, ZiniPay, PayTiller, BengaliPay, Payora BD, SohojPay BD, EasyPayWay, AK Pay, BD PAY, ShajgarPay, AsthaPay/CPay, UddoktaPay, Walletmix, BttPay, Easy Pay Automation, UniquePay BD, BD AUTO PAY, RH Pay BD, EzePay, AutoPay Ltd, Biswasto, and PipraPay.
The central bank advised all individuals, institutions, and businesses to refrain from conducting transactions with or engaging in the operations of these unlicensed payment aggregators to avoid legal penalties and financial risks.
Regulatory actions leading up to this notice have targeted unauthorized digital apps and platforms involved in high-interest online micro-lending, illegal gambling, and financial fraud.
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) and Bangladesh Bank routinely instruct commercial banks and mobile financial services (MFS) to suspend transaction channels for unauthorized platforms that bypass central bank supervision, endanger consumer data, or engage in predatory lending practices.
In July 2024, the Parliament passed the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, significantly strengthening Bangladesh Bank's statutory authority to oversee non-bank digital financial services.
Under Section 4(2) and Section 15(2) of the Act, operating any payment platform, digital wallet, or online transaction gateway without explicit authorization from Bangladesh Bank is illegal.
The law introduced strict penalties under Section 37(1), declaring unlicensed financial operations a cognizable, non-bailable offense punishable by imprisonment, steep fines, or both.
Certain platforms listed in the notice had previously faced regulatory action. For instance, Bangladesh Bank officially canceled the Payment System Operator (PSO) license of Walletmix Limited in November 2023 after detecting unauthorized and illegal financial transactions that violated regulatory terms.
Despite losing its license, platforms attempting to operate or offer payment aggregator tools without authorization remain subject to enforcement.
The Payment Systems Supervision Department launched these sweeps to mitigate systemic risks in the digital ecosystem.
Unregistered payment aggregators and gateways often lack mandatory Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) safeguards, exposing consumers and merchants to risk of financial loss, delayed settlements, data breaches, and illegal fund diversion.

item.title: Standard Chartered Bangladesh, ICAB unveil priority banking for chartered accountants
item.description:
Standard Chartered Bangladesh has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB) to introduce an exclusive Priority Banking proposition for eligible ICAB members.
Chartered Accountants play a vital role in ensuring good governance, transparency, sustainable growth and bring positive changes to the economy.
Designed to recognize the contribution of Chartered Accountants, this proposition brings together a suite of customized financial and lifestyle benefits for this esteemed professional community.
Subject to applicable terms and conditions, eligible Chartered Accountants can now enjoy a range of preferential banking and financing solutions, including savings on ICAB membership and practitioner fees, cashback and fee waivers on selected products, curated lifestyle and travel privileges, along complimentary supplementary debit cards.
Under this partnership, eligible ICAB members will also have access to Standard Chartered’s broader Priority Banking proposition, including dedicated Relationship Manager support, access to Bancassurance solutions, and Islamic Banking solutions through Standard Chartered Saadiq.
Enamul Huque, CEO Officer, Standard Chartered Bangladesh, said: “Chartered Accountants are an esteemed group of professionals who play a critical role in ensuring good governance and transparency and in safeguarding the business, and policy framework; not only in Bangladesh, but across the world. Our partnership with ICAB recognizes this important contribution. Through this proposition, we aim to offer them convenience, meaningful value and a tailored banking experience in managing their personal finances.”
Sabbir Ahmed, president, ICAB, said: “Delivering value to our members remains an important priority for ICAB. We welcome this collaboration with Standard Chartered, which brings together benefits that address both the professional and personal financial needs of Chartered Accountants. The banking and financing benefits will help members manage their financial priorities with greater flexibility. We look forward to our members benefiting from this partnership and making full use of the proposition.”
The MoU was signed by Enamul Huque, chief executive officer, Standard Chartered Bangladesh and Sabbir Ahmed, president, ICAB.
Senior representatives from both organizations were also present at the ceremony.

item.title: JCI Dhaka Sparks convenes 3rd general members' meeting 2026
item.description:
JCI Dhaka Sparks convened its 3rd General Members' Meeting (GMM) of 2026 on September 26 at the Sirajul Alam Khan Centre and Research Institute in Dhaka.
Local President Raihan Ahmed Dip chaired the assembly, which gathered over 75% of the board of directors alongside national leaders and visiting chapter presidents.
A primary highlight of the meeting was the official launch of the "Green Village" climate initiative.
Presented by director Sahaduzzaman Shrabon, the project aims to tackle deforestation and biomass loss in the Chittagong Division by replacing traditional firewood cookstoves with IoT-enabled eCook Induction Stoves from clean-tech partner ATEC.
Real-time carbon reduction data from the stoves will be verified under Gold Standard accreditation standards.
Local President Raihan Ahmed Dip announced a national Memorandum of Understanding with Hajj with Ayesha, granting all active JCI Bangladesh members a minimum 10% discount on administrative and service fees, as well as special package and ticket privileges.
Earlier, the chapter co-organized a training session on JCI Discover and JCI Explore alongside JCI Dhaka Astral and JCI Dhaka Young.
Conducted by NEVP Shahmina Isha Mannan, the session saw over 40 young leaders complete their core modules.
Six new members were inducted into the chapter: Mir Sadman Ali, Dr. Nazmun Nahar Hafsa, Fatema Tuz Zannat Bristy, Md. Samiul Haque, Tasnuva Rahman Nishim (Opshori), and Abrar Farhan Zaman.
Exceptional performance was recognized with Member of the Month crests presented to ASM Mosabbir Tanim (July), Tasnuva Rahman Nishim (August), and Moumita Siddika (September).
Special recognition was also given to past local president senator Noor E Alam Bhuiyan.
Activity and treasury reports were adopted, covering past projects such as Fight the Bite and PASC 2026.
Members were encouraged to prepare for upcoming events, including the 2026 TOYP Banquet at Radisson Blu Water Garden Hotel on October 17 and the 2026 JCI World Congress in Clark, Philippines, from November 11–15.

item.title: NRB Bank, MetLife renew partnership for 8th consecutive year
item.description:
NRB Bank PLC has renewed its partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth consecutive year to provide enhanced insurance protection benefits for eligible credit cardholders.
Under the agreement, the bank's eligible credit cardholders will receive insurance coverage designed to help settle the outstanding balance on their credit cards in the event of death or permanent disability, subject to policy terms and conditions.
Eligible cardholders will also be entitled to an In-Hospital Cash Benefit for each hospitalization, helping them manage medical expenses during treatment and recovery.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, and Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, has signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, said: "Our customers expect banking services that add meaningful value to their everyday lives. Our partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth year will allow eligible credit cardholders to continue benefiting from insurance protection designed to support them and their families during difficult and unexpected situations."
Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, said: "Financial protection can make an important difference during an unexpected health crisis or other unforeseen event. By continuing our partnership with NRB Bank PLC, we aim to provide impactful insurance benefits that can help reduce financial worries and support greater peace of mind."
NRB Bank is one of the leading providers of card issuance and digital financial services in Bangladesh.
The bank serves customers through multiple channels, including digital banking, branch banking, agent banking, and internet banking, and offers a diversified range of modern, technology-driven banking products and services to meet customers' evolving needs.
MetLife Bangladesh, which has been operating in the country since 1952, currently serves more than one million individual customers and over 900 corporate clients.
The company continues to maintain its leadership position among life insurers in Bangladesh in claims settlement, paying Tk2,853 crore in claims in 2025 and Tk1,384 crore during the first six months of 2026, the highest claims payouts in the industry for the respective periods.
MetLife Bangladesh also maintained a claims settlement ratio of 98% in 2025, one of the highest in the industry.
Senior officials from NRB Bank PLC and MetLife Bangladesh attended the signing ceremony.

item.title: UCB’s ARFL wins ‘Project of the Year’ award for digital innovation
item.description:
United Commercial Bank PLC (UCB) has achieved a significant milestone in its digital transformation journey as its Agri Rural Fast Loan (ARFL) initiative has been named Champion Project of the Year, Information Technology (Medium Category) at the Bangladesh Project Management Symposium & Awards 2026.
The event was recently organized by the Project Management Institute (PMI), Bangladesh Chapter, at a hotel in the capital.
State Minister of Planning Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki attended the event as chief guest.
Deputy managing director & chief operating officer of UCB Md Abdullah Al Mamoon was present at the event along with other senior officials of the bank.
ARFL represents UCB’s commitment to making financing faster, simpler and more accessible through technology.
The initiative is designed to facilitate agricultural loan disbursement to eligible farmers within a single day.
The recognition of ARFL represents an important milestone in UCB’s broader digital transformation journey and showcases the capabilities of UCB ONE- UCB’s Core digital banking platform and technology foundation for delivering integrated, scalable and customer-centric financial services.
Commenting on the recognition, UCB highlighted the award as a proud milestone for the bank specially an agriculture and rural entrepreneurship initiative and an affirmation of its ongoing efforts to harness digital innovation for more efficient and inclusive financial services.

item.title: CEC: Thakurgaon-1 by election to gain acclamation as well
item.description:
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin on Sunday said the upcoming Thakurgaon-1 parliamentary by-election will be held in a praiseworthy manner, like the February-12 national election.
“Insha'Allah, I can guarantee that just as we conducted the 13th parliamentary election—which earned acclamation both at home and abroad—you will similarly appreciate the way this one (by-election) is held,” he said.
The CEC made the remarks while talking to reporters after visiting the monitoring cell set up at Nirbachan Bhaban to monitor the Thakurgaon-1 by-election in real time from the capital.
He said all necessary measures have been taken to arrange the Thakurgaon-1 by-polls in a fair manner, which is scheduled to be held on November 29 next.
Nasir Uddin said an adequate number of law enforcement personnel will be deployed to maintain law and order in the parliamentary by-election.
He said the monitoring cell will work for the Thakurgaon-1 by-election in exactly the same way as it did during the 13th parliamentary election. “We will monitor it centrally so that we can intervene in the right manner at the right time,” he added.
The CEC said the overall environment in the election field is currently very good.
According to the election schedule announced by the EC, the deadline for submission of nomination papers expired on Sunday afternoon (5pm) in the by-election.
The nomination papers will be scrutinised on Sept 29, while the last date for withdrawal of candidature is Oct 7, and voting will be held on Oct 29 from 8am to 4pm.
Meanwhile, the EC held a meeting with representatives of law enforcement agencies at Nirbachan Bhaban on Sunday afternoon ahead of the by-election.
Other election commissioners attended the meeting chaired by CEC AMM Nasir Uddin.
Asked about the meeting, the CEC said an adequate number of law enforcement personnel would remain deployed in the field to keep the law and order situation fully under control during the election.

item.title: Dengue: Six more die as 2,158 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Six people died of dengue while 2,158 new cases were reported in Bangladesh in the 24 hours till Sunday morning.
These are the highest single-day cases so far from the mosquito-borne disease this year.
The latest fatalities have brought the number of dengue deaths in the country to 225 this year, while the new cases raised the total number of infections to73,694, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the new deaths, two deaths were reported in Khulna division while one each in Barisal, Chittagong, Dhaka divisions and Dhaka South City Corporation.
Of the total deaths recorded this year, 46.4% were men and 53.6% were women.
Earlier on September 8, Bangladesh recorded its highest number of dengue deaths in a single day this year, with nine people succumbing to the mosquito-borne disease.
The previous highest daily tally of dengue cases was recorded on September 14 with 1,733 patients being hospitalized across the country.
Meanwhile, 68,006 dengue patients have been discharged from hospitals after recovery, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Shahe Alam stresses ensuring solar power use in govt offices, institutions
item.description:
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development, and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, MP, on Sunday urged the relevant departments and agencies to work in a coordinated manner to ensure the use of solar power in government offices and institutions quickly.
“The relevant departments and agencies should advance their work according to their respective action plans and regularly review the progress of implementation,” he said, mentioning that the activities to use solar power must be implemented quickly.
He made the call at a meeting held in the conference room of the Rural Development and Cooperatives Division at the Secretariat, said a PID release.
He also said he would soon inspect the activities on the ground to install solar power at various institutions.
At the meeting, the ongoing activities and implementation progress of action plans of the concerned departments and agencies were reviewed to increase the use of solar power in government offices and institutions.
Various aspects of reducing electricity costs of government institutions and expanding the use of renewable energy through increased use of solar power were also discussed.
The meeting stressed taking necessary initiatives to implement action plans for using solar power at field-level offices of respective agencies as well as offices and institutions located in Dhaka.
Rural Development and Cooperatives Division Secretary Dr Rafiqul Mohamad chaired the meeting.
Managing Director of Small Farmers Development Foundation Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman, Director General of Bangladesh Academy for Rural Development; Comilla Saif Uddin Ahmed, Registrar and Director General of the Department of Cooperatives; Md Selim Fakir, Director General of Bangladesh Rural Development Board; AKM Tarek; and heads of various departments and agencies under the ministry were present at the meeting.
Heads of various departments and agencies located outside Dhaka also joined the meeting online and presented the activities and progress of their respective institutions.

item.title: Singapore wants to provide border security assistance to Bangladesh
item.description:
Outgoing Singaporean Chargé d’Affaires has expressed his country’s interest in providing modern technology and technical assistance to strengthen Bangladesh’s border and immigration security.
Outgoing Chargé d’Affaires of Singapore Mitchel Lee said this during a courtesy call on Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed at his Home Ministry office in the Bangladesh Secretariat on Sunday, a PID handout said.
During the meeting, they discussed the issues of bilateral relations, capacity building of the Bangladesh Police, modernization of security systems at airports and land ports, technology transfer, economic and trade cooperation, and other issues of mutual interest.
Lee highlighted Singapore’s willingness to support Bangladesh in adopting modern technology for border and immigration security, as well as providing technical assistance in these areas.
He said bilateral relations and trade between Bangladesh and Singapore were continuing to expand.
Ahmed also expressed hope that the appointment of a full-fledged Singaporean high commissioner to Bangladesh would be completed soon to further strengthen bilateral trade and relations.
Ahmed emphasized on the longstanding diplomatic and economic ties between the two countries.
He said Bangladesh government is working to establish modern, technology-based immigration and border security systems in the frontier and airports.
The minister also expressed hope that cooperation between the two countries would expand through joint efforts to combat extremism, police training and transfer of technologies.
Singapore’s incoming Chargé d’Affaires Philip Ong, Additional Secretary of the Political and Immigration Wing of the Home Ministry Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, and Second Secretary of the Singapore mission Dhanya Lingesh were present.

item.title: Riaz Hamidullah: Dhaka-Delhi ties 'organic', conversation must continue
item.description:
Outgoing Bangladesh High Commissioner to India M Riaz Hamidullah has described the relationship between Bangladesh and India as “organic” and rooted in mutual interdependence and shared interests.
“Very simple - this is a relationship which, on several occasions, I've said is organic ... of mutual interdependence. It's a relationship which is in shared interests,” he said.
Hamidullah, who assumed charge as Bangladesh High Commissioner to India on April 7, 2025, is set to leave New Delhi early next month to take up his new assignment as Permanent Representative of Bangladesh to the United Nations in Geneva, a senior official said.
The diplomat said differences in views, perspectives and approaches are natural in any close relationship particularly between two countries that share an intimate geography.
“But with those, we must remain engaged; carry on conversation, as we need to unpack the interaction between people far more than it is today,” he told Indian media ANI in an interview.
He said people-to-people engagement should go beyond conventional exchanges, noting that broader interaction could reach millions of people and help strengthen understanding between the two countries.
“That’s an unattended space that remains,” he said, referring to the need for greater engagement at the people-to-people level.
While communication between ministries and governments remains important, Hamidullah said he sees a much larger space that can be addressed through broader social and educational engagement.
“For example, among students, school-going children and universities,” the envoy said, adding that greater engagement in these areas could reach “millions” of people and make a “distinct difference” to the relationship between the two countries.
Reflecting on his recent experiences in India, Hamidullah, in a post on his verified X account, spoke about a visit during which an interaction with students at Delhi Public School (DPS) Srinagar left a lasting impression on him.
He visited the school after arriving in Srinagar on September 3, saying he was particularly struck by its inclusive and scholastic environment and the energy of its more than 5,000 students.
DPS Srinagar was founded in 2003 by Vijay K Dhar under the D P Dhar Memorial Trust. The Dhar family has longstanding links with Bangladesh, including through the late D P Dhar, who played a significant role in the formation and early years of Bangladesh.
Hamidullah said his interaction with students at the school offered him a different perspective on how young people view issues such as borders and identity.
A Class XII student, RJ Fatima, introduced herself to him as a radio jockey and invited him to the school's digital radio station, which, he said, has been operating since 2019.
“She just asked me and got me into her radio studio, and we got into conversation,” Hamidullah recalled. What surprised him most, he said, was Fatima’s question: “How do you look at borders?”
“Imagine, sitting in Srinagar, a girl asking this,” he said, adding that he took the question in “absolute candour” and responded to her openly.
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi recently called for keeping trade, cultural exchanges and people-to-people connectivity between Bangladesh and India moving forward, saying such issues should not be held back by political developments.
Talking to reporters after a cultural program in Dhaka earlier this month, he said the two countries would continue discussing various issues, but matters such as the Maitree Express, the Ganges Water Treaty, trade and cultural exchanges should not be allowed to get stuck.
“These are the things of ordinary people,” said the High Commissioner, highlighting the importance of keeping people at the center.
The High Commissioner said trade restrictions on both sides have to be eased. Otherwise, he noted, people will suffer.
He said there is no need to rush and the political process will take its own course. But the work that concerns ordinary people must continue, Trivedi said.
India on Tuesday reiterated that it wants to take its relationship with Bangladesh forward in a positive, constructive and forward-looking manner and expressed its willingness to discuss all bilateral issues between the two countries.
“India desires a positive, constructive, and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh,” Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said while responding to a question about bilateral ties during a media briefing in New Delhi.
Jaiswal said India is ready to discuss all bilateral issues with Bangladesh through the existing structured mechanisms.
“Our intent is to take this relationship forward in a positive direction, in a constructive direction, in a forward-looking manner,” he said.
A vibrant ‘Ilish Fest’ celebrating Bangladesh’s national fish, Ilish, was held at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi on Saturday.
The event, held at the “Maitri” Auditorium of the High Commission, brought together prominent Indian politicians, diplomats, civil society representatives, academics, journalists and cultural personalities.
During the festival, prominent Indian personalities unveiled the book A Fish Called Ilish, published in Dhaka.
The event centred on Ilish, which is deeply rooted in Bengali heritage, culture and culinary traditions. It also provided an opportunity to showcase Bangladesh’s rich cultural heritage and hospitality, with guests enjoying a variety of Ilish dishes alongside traditional Bangladeshi cuisine.
The guests appreciated not only the distinct taste of Bangladeshi Ilish but also the emotions, traditions and cultural values associated with the fish.
Former Indian Minister of State for External Affairs and noted journalist M J Akbar, former diplomat and politician Mani Shankar Aiyar, human rights activist and social thinker Syeda Hameed, former Indian ambassador Ronen Sen, eminent sociologist Ashis Nandy and other distinguished personalities attended the program.
The guests praised the taste of Bangladeshi Ilish and the overall organization of the festival.
The event also highlighted Bangladesh’s heritage, culture and hospitality, while guests expressed hope that such initiatives would contribute to further strengthening the friendly ties between the peoples of Bangladesh and India.
Speaking after the book launch, Bangladesh High Commissioner Riaz Hamidullah said Ilish is closely linked to Bangladesh’s identity and the fish is deeply intertwined with the country’s social and economic fabric.
The High Commissioner also noted that Bangladesh has five Ilish sanctuaries and that the government has taken various initiatives to increase Ilish breeding and production. These efforts have contributed to increased conservation and production of Ilish, he said.

item.title: Cavan Sullivan makes USA debut at 16 after brothers’ Bangladesh stint
item.description:
Cavan Sullivan has made his United States senior international debut, adding another chapter to a remarkable football story that recently saw his twin brothers represent and win a title with Bangladesh at the U-20 level.
The 16-year-old Philadelphia Union midfielder started for the USA in their 4-1 victory over Peru in Orlando on Saturday, two days before his 17th birthday. His debut made him the fourth-youngest player to appear for the United States senior national team and the youngest in more than two decades, since Freddy Adu in 2006.
Sullivan played 62 minutes and showed the attacking creativity and confidence that have made him one of the most closely watched young players in Major League Soccer. Although he did not score or register an assist, he was involved in several attacking moves and produced an encouraging performance as the USA began a new cycle following the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
“What a pinch-me moment,” Sullivan said after the match. “I’ve been dreaming of this moment since I was so young. This means so much to me and my family, and it’s an extreme honor to represent my country.”
The occasion also offered another international milestone for the Sullivan family, whose connection with Bangladesh football has grown significantly in recent months.
Cavan’s twin brothers, Ronan and Declan Sullivan, represented Bangladesh at the 2026 SAFF U-20 Championship in the Maldives after becoming eligible through their maternal Bangladeshi heritage.
Ronan made an immediate impact, scoring both goals in Bangladesh’s 2-0 victory over Pakistan in the group stage. Bangladesh subsequently reached the final against India, which ended goalless after 90 minutes before Bangladesh prevailed 4-3 on penalties to win the SAFF U-20 title.
Ronan converted Bangladesh’s decisive fifth penalty, while Declan was also part of the championship-winning campaign.
The family’s footballing story has therefore taken an unusual international turn. While Ronan and Declan have already celebrated a regional championship wearing Bangladesh colours, their younger brother has now begun his senior international career with the United States.
Cavan’s rapid rise has been equally notable. He made his professional debut for Philadelphia Union at just 14 and has since established himself as one of the most exciting young players in American football.
His USA debut came as coach Mauricio Pochettino used the post-World Cup friendlies to introduce a new generation of players. For the Sullivan family, however, the moment carried an additional significance: three brothers have now represented two different national teams on the international stage, with Bangladesh playing a particularly memorable role in the family’s football journey.

item.title: Mbappe diagnosed with knee hyperextension injury, out for two weeks
item.description:
Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe has been diagnosed with a hyperextension injury to the posterior capsule of his left knee, the Spanish club said Saturday.
Mbappe suffered the injury during France’s 1-0 Nations League victory over Turkey on Friday, leaving the field shortly after scoring his record-extending 67th international goal.
France coach Zinedine Zidane had earlier said the initial prognosis was “not good.”
Real Madrid confirmed the injury after medical tests on Saturday but did not provide a recovery timeline or specify the treatment planned for the forward.
“After the tests carried out today on our player Kylian Mbappe by Real Madrid’s Medical Services, he has been diagnosed with a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee,” the club said in a statement.
New France coach Zinedine Zidane said France were "not going to take any risks" and that he would not use Mbappe in the three Nations League matches scheduled over the next 10 days.
France travel to Belgium on Monday before hosting Italy and Belgium at the Stade de France on October 2 and 5.
Real Madrid's first game after the international break, with Villarreal on October 10, might be too soon for an Mbappe return but Spanish daily AS reported Saturday he would certainly be ready for the Classico with Barcelona October 25.

item.title: Tuchel to 'keep pushing' England to reach Spain's level
item.description:
Thomas Tuchel remains convinced England can get over the line against the world's best despite seeing his side blow a second-half lead to lose 3-2 to Spain on Saturday.
The world champions were headed for a first competitive defeat in three-and-a-half years as England led 2-1 at half-time and then missed the chance to add to their lead when Harry Kane's penalty rattled off the woodwork.
But two sloppy defensive errors cost Tuchel's men for both Spain's first two goals.
Marc Guehi was caught in possession by Lamine Yamal for the visitors' early opener before Nico O'Reilly's wayward pass that led to Alex Baena's equaliser swung momentum back in Spain's direction.
Mikel Oyarzabal then completed the comeback by scoring the winner, just as he did when the sides met in the final of Euro 2024.
Defeat means England have won just six of their last 16 matches against opponents ranked in FIFA's top 10.
"I was not in charge for these 16 matches, for sure not and I think we did everything today to beat Spain," said Tuchel.
"Details matter on this kind of level. Like I said, the amount of clear-cut mistakes was too high on our side today, unfortunately, and in the last 20 metres they were more composed and more clinical to convert our ball-losses into clear-cut chances."
Tuchel was seeking a response to silence his critics for a series of defensive-minded substitutions as England also surrendered a lead to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals.
This time there was no lack of ambition in a wildly open encounter, but Tuchel conceded that England are still not able to produce consistently for 90 minutes.
"We will keep on pushing this team," added Tuchel.
"We proved it at the World Cup that we are capable to do it in tournaments. Today we cannot prove it in the result, but I think the way we played was enough to beat them."
England now face a double header against the Czech Republic either side of a trip to Croatia over the next 10 days.

item.title: Solid-state batteries are finally breaking the "five years away" curse
item.description:
For over a decade, EV batteries kept promising more than they delivered.
You've probably heard "solid-state is five years away" so many times it's practically a punchline. But 2026 feels different.
Chinese, American, and German manufacturers are all reporting real advances at once, and for once it doesn't look like empty hype.
So, what's changed?
In a normal EV, lithium ions swim through a liquid electrolyte between electrodes.
Solid-state batteries swap that liquid for something solid, paired with a lithium-metal anode instead of the usual graphite.
Small swap, big consequences.
Take energy density.
The best lithium-ion batteries today max out around 200-300 Wh/kg.
Solid-state cells are already hitting 400-500 Wh/kg.
More than double the energy per kilogram--with manufacturers eyeing 500-600 Wh/kg in the next few years.
Safety matters just as much.
Liquid electrolytes tend to grow dendrites--tiny metal splinters that pierce the battery's internal walls and cause short circuits, sometimes fires.
Solid electrolytes choke that growth down.
Some of these cells have literally been stabbed with a nail in testing and just... didn't catch fire.
China is way out ahead.
Greater Bay Technology, backed by GAC Group, rolled its first all-solid-state cells off the line in April.
No liquid electrolyte, and they shrugged off needle punctures, extrusion, and thermal shock without igniting, hitting 260-500 Wh/kg with fast charging built in.
GBT wants GWh-scale production before the year's out--faster than its own parent company GAC, whose internal roadmap plays it safer, targeting 2027-2030.
Chery's chasing the same line. In September, it said real-world testing of its all-solid-state batteries starts in 2027, with a hybrid version landing in cars even sooner.
One cell hits 400 Wh/kg; a polymer version claims 600 Wh/kg--theoretically over 1,500 kilometres per charge, though real-world range will land lower than that lab number.
Legacy players are moving more cautiously.
Mercedes-Benz has been road-testing a solid-state pack with U.S. partner Factorial since early 2025, around 450 Wh/kg.
In their actual test car-- a modified EQS --that's roughly 25% more range for the same battery weight, pushing past 1,000 kilometres.
Factorial's own marketing claims the underlying cell tech could offer up to 80% more range than typical lithium-ion --but that's a claim about the cell generally, not something the EQS itself has shown on the road.
Either way, nothing here hits showrooms before the late 2020s.
Toyota and Nissan are running similar programmes quietly in the background.
For an actual buyer, this mostly means less range anxiety. Today's EVs get 250-350 miles per charge, a few premium ones nearing 400.
Solid-state could stretch that another 20-40%, and a few manufacturers are already trialling mid-size EVs clearing 400 miles.
The catch is money. These batteries are still expensive to build, so expect the first generation to cost more before prices settle.
Bangladesh's EV market is tiny, but cost and range are exactly the numbers that'll decide when that changes-- and as battery tech races ahead globally, the job market of the near future might get shaped as much by battery labs as by software.
None of this means solid-state EVs are flooding the market tomorrow.
Building them reliably and cheaply at a real scale is still a genuinely hard problem. The same one that's kept this tech at "five years away" for so long.
Most analysts expect hybrid batteries first, as a stepping stone, with full solid-state becoming common between the late 2020s and early 2030s.
EVTank's most recent report, from this July, puts global shipments at 607.2 GWh by 2030, with fully solid-state cells making up around a fifth of that--a touch more modest than earlier forecasts, but still a serious bet.
Keep an eye on 2027, not for full mass production, but for the wave of real-world testing that Chery, GAC, CATL, BYD, and others are all circling.
Whoever gets there first, the thing that's been missing to make EVs as easy as filling up a patrol car doesn't look far off anymore.
It's happening and moving fast.
Zahin is a 9th grader chronically curious about batteries, gadgets, and anything faster than it should be.

item.title: ‘Do something’: Salman Muqtadir tells home minister
item.description:
YouTuber Salman Muqtadir, whose studio was damaged in an attack and vandalism, has said he does not need any compensation. He can rebuild his life on his own. But the government must ensure the safety and security of every person in the country. Otherwise, the country will suffer greatly.

He made the remarks in a video message on Sunday afternoon in response to Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed’s comments about the attack on his studio. Addressing the home minister, Salman said he should “do something” to ensure the safety of people in the country if he could. There was no need to spread misleading information about him, he said.

Criticising the home minister’s remarks in the video message, Salman Muqtadir said he had waited at a police station until 4am after the attack on his studio last night to file a case, but the police did not take it. The home minister later said at a briefing in the afternoon that no case had been filed.

Attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio: 3 accused sent to jail, remand hearing on Wednesday

He also questioned why a case had not been filed until the video of the incident went viral and the home minister made his statement. He asked why he had been unable to file a case despite waiting at the police station with several people until 4am. Even after the case was eventually filed, he questioned why the information had not reached the home minister.

Addressing the home minister, Salman Muqtadir said, “With the enormous responsibility you have, when you said in your statement that a case had not been filed and that Salman Muqtadir had not filed a case, why did you make this ridiculous statement and make your entire department and government look so small?”

He said, “I was sitting at your police station with so many people until 4am last night, at the Cantonment police station. I returned home exhausted, at a time when I was not supposed to be in the right state of mind. Even then, no case was filed until this afternoon. Until things went viral and your statement came out, why was the case not filed even though I had gone there? This is a question I should be asking you. You have to answer the people of the country why a case was not filed under Salahuddin Ahmed.”

Asked when the case was filed, Cantonment police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Gias Uddin told Prothom Alo on Sunday night that the case was filed at 8:30am that day.

Salman Muqtadir also addressed the home minister’s claim at an afternoon briefing that no case had been filed. Addressing him, Salman said, “You are the home minister. Every police station, every authority and every administration is under your command, under one call, one button. You don’t even know that a case has been filed. You don’t have the update. How detached are you from the citizens of your country, from your own safety and security protocol? You are completely detached. You don’t know that a case has been filed.”

Attack on Salman Muqtadir’s studio: ‘Vandals entered New Gini Properties firing shots’

The home minister described Salman Muqtadir’s allegations of extortion against the BNP in connection with the incident as “broad-brush and controversial”. Criticising the minister’s remarks, Salman said, “Why did I mention BNP? Why did I mention extortion? The way you give that little smile, I feel like giving the same smile now. Look, I smile too, and you smile too. We are helpless in the same way. You can’t do anything, and I can’t do anything either. You are laughing it off, and I’m laughing it off too.”

Salman Muqtadir claimed that the three people detained from the scene last night were the ones who mentioned the BNP. In the video, he said, “Shots were fired from their guns. Evidence has been collected. Their machetes, shovels—all have been collected. I saw the videos on their phones. I saw their faces. They are admitting it. After being beaten by people and hearing what people were saying, they took the name of BNP.”

Criticising the home minister in this regard, Salman Muqtadir further said, “I have to maintain my sanity, maintain my composure, and then keep my speech in order. I cannot say anything against BNP or point a finger at them. I am very confused. Have you taken responsibility for BNP’s PR management crisis, or have you taken responsibility for the Home Ministry? I am very confused. Because the problem was safety and security.”

Addressing the home minister, Salman Muqtadir further said, “We are not here to ask you to investigate. We are here for action. You yourself said that I was making broad-brush allegations. Then you yourself said that someone from a military force was involved here. Okay, you investigated that person. Then what did you do? You came to the press briefing and gave no answer, took no action, and did nothing that could assure the people of Bangladesh of their security. Instead, you said, ‘Salman Muqtadir said this, the gentleman said that, he said this and that.’

Salman Muqtadir said, “Do something. We are not asking you for money. You don’t have to rebuild my studio. I, Salman Muqtadir, am strong enough. I will not beg anyone. … I don’t need anything. If you really want to do something, do something for Bangladesh.”

He said, “If, through this incident, you cannot ensure any kind of safety and security for people, if you cannot ensure the security of my fellow citizens, then that’s my loss.”

item.title: Attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio: 3 accused sent to jail, remand hearing on Wednesday
item.description:
A request has been made for a five-day remand for three suspects arrested in a case of unauthorised entry, vandalism, looting, and theft at content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio.

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Arifur Rahman has scheduled a hearing for 30th September and ordered the suspects to be sent to jail.

Today, Sunday, the investigation officer of the case, Inspector Subrata Debnath of Cantonment Police Station, produced the suspects in court and requested a five-day remand.

Prosecution Department's SI Tarequr Rahman told Prothom Alo that the suspects sent to jail are Md Mamun (32), Md. Aslam (24), and Munna (29).

Inspector Subrata Debnath of Cantonment Police Station, the investigation officer, told Prothom Alo, the plaintiff of the case is Saiful Islam, the director of Newgini Project.

There are 13 named suspects in the case, among whom the court has sent three to jail. Their political affiliation is not yet known. Salman Muqtadir has not filed a separate case regarding the incident.

According to the case details, approximately 50 miscreants illegally entered the project area of 'Newgini Properties Limited' in West Matikata, Cantonment Police Station, on Saturday.

During this time, they fired around 50 rounds randomly and attacked with machetes, knives, and sticks. Several people, including site engineer Md Parvez, were seriously injured.

Unauthorised entry, vandalism, and looting occurred at Salman Muqtadir's 'Brown Fish' studio during this time.

The complaint also states that the attackers looted a large amount of goods, including cash, laptops, computers, BRB cables, cameras, and professional media equipment, from the project area.

Moreover, vehicles were vandalised, resulting in a reported loss of approximately Tk 14.28 million, and goods worth Tk 15. 44 million were stolen.

Upon hearing the incident, the Cantonment Police rushed to the scene, at which point the attackers also fired at the police. The police, in self-defence and to control the situation, fired five rounds from a shotgun.

Two suspects named in the complaint were arrested from the scene. Later, another was apprehended through further operations. Police have reported recovering local weapons and shell casings from the arrested suspects.

item.title: Civil Society Organisation Alliance condemns attack on Radda health centre
item.description:
The CSO Alliance, a national coalition of more than 300 non-government and civil society organisations, strongly condemns the looting and demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1, Dhaka, on the night of 24 September, reports a press release.

A group of 200 to 250 men held the clinic’s security guards hostage, looted vaccines, medicines, equipment and cash, and razed the centre’s buildings with heavy machinery. The CSO Alliance stands with Radda’s staff and all the families who depend on the centre and demands a prompt, impartial and effective investigation, accountability for those responsible, and compensation for Radda’s losses.

Radda, a Mirpur-based NGO health centre set up in 1974 by Radda Barnen (Save the Children Sweden), has for about five decades provided vaccination, maternal care and family planning to poor mothers and children, in partnership with the Government. Its Mirpur-1 clinic was attacked just before the second phase of the national measles-rubella campaign was due to start. It is continuing to vaccinate children in makeshift tarpaulin tents, but has had to stop most other services.

The people of Bangladesh expected the newly elected Government to provide greater protection from mob violence and lawlessness, and to ensure effective justice. Unfortunately, these problems continue, and this attack is one more example of that ongoing concern. Land disputes must be resolved through legal processes, not by force in the middle of the night.

Partnership between the Government, businesses and NGOs in economic activity and service delivery depends on the maintenance of law and order. NGOs have long worked alongside the state in health.

The CSO Alliance’s study on 50 years of civil society in Bangladesh shows how this partnership helped expand child immunisation, which stood at just two per cent in 1985. Today, 81.6 per cent of children are fully immunised, according to the latest EPI Coverage Evaluation Survey (2023). Everyone needs legal protection from extortion, vandalism and forcible occupation.

The CSO welcome the nine arrests and the recovery of looted goods so far, the announcement of a police inquiry into the role of its officers, and the Health Minister’s assurance that ownership will be decided by the court and that vaccination will continue.

The CSO call on the Government to:

1. Ensure a prompt, impartial and effective investigation to identify those who planned, financed or took part in the attack, regardless of political identity, and ensure accountability.

2. Publish the findings of the police inquiry and information on action taken against any person found responsible.

3. Ensure security for the Radda clinic to operate, and compensation for its losses.

4. Help Radda move its vaccination and other services from the makeshift tents to a safe temporary facility, and replace the lost vaccines and supplies, so that no child in the area misses the measlesrubella campaign, which ends on 31 October.

5. Protect all health facilities, NGOs and businesses from extortion, vandalism and forcible occupation, and treat any attack on a health facility as an emergency.
